plan.notes: Source: 'BS in Computer Science Curriculum' table, p. 186 of the official 2025-2026 Announcement of the UCLA Henry Samueli School of Engineering and Applied Science (published October 1, 2025), retrieved 2026-09-30 from https://www.seasoasa.ucla.edu/wp-content/uploads/seasoasa/UCLASamueli-Anncmt-25-26.pdf. Catalog year: the 2026-2027 Announcement was not yet published as of 2026-09-30, so this plan is transcribed from the latest published official catalog; OASA's Computer Science Worksheets page (https://www.seasoasa.ucla.edu/computer-science-worksheets/) confirms the Fall 2025 catalog changes (removal of COM SCI 118 and M152A as required courses; 28 units / seven CS electives; M148 no longer a CS elective) remain the current Computer Science BS requirements. Transcription method: manual, course-by-course transcription of the printed quarter-by-quarter curriculum table (12 quarters: Fall/Winter/Spring over four years); every course code, title, and unit value is verbatim from the table and per-quarter sums were recomputed and verified against the table's stated TOTAL of 181 units (verified sum 181). IMPORTANT CAVEAT — internal inconsistency in the official document: the printed curriculum table places COM SCI 118 (Computer Network Fundamentals) in Junior-year 1st quarter and omits COM SCI 180, but the same Announcement's 'The Major' requirements text for Computer Science BS (p. 81) requires COM SCI 180 (Introduction to Algorithms and Complexity) among the five required courses (111, 131, 180, 181, M151B/M116C), and OASA's official Fall 2025 catalog-change summary states COM SCI 118 was REMOVED as a required course. The table is transcribed exactly as printed; students should confirm the 118-vs-180 placement against the CS worksheet for their catalog year and an OASA counselor. Placeholder slots (Computer Science Elective, Probability Elective, Science and Technology Elective, Technical Breadth Course, UCLA Samueli GE Elective, UCLA Samueli Ethics Course) are student-choice courses from OASA-approved lists — see the Announcement's elective lists and footnotes. Per-course prerequisites are not given in the curriculum table; they appear in the Announcement's course descriptions. OASA notes that individual student plans built from the CS worksheet are tentative and vary by student; this table is the school's published sample 4-year sequence ('the 4 yr plan in the back of the Announcement' referenced by OASA).
